Sara,

Following our kickoff last week, we're scheduling a 4-hour verification sprint for the on-prem release (VPC/private control plane) to validate stability, telemetry, and the canary rollback exercise.

Proposed window: 2026-03-22 18:00-22:00 PT
Goals:
- Execute runbook playback (sanity checks + dependency validations)
- Run canary traffic at 10% for 30 minutes, validate latency/p95 and error budgets
- Perform a simulated rollback (dry-run + one actual rollback to validate automation)
- Confirm KV cache warm-up and prefix caching behavior under real traffic

Attachments: release-sanity-checklist.md, canary-rollback-playbook.pdf
Pre-reqs we need from Kestrel:
- Maintenance window confirmation on your side
- Short-term KMS key escrow note: will your security team be available if we rotate keys for the test?

I'm looping Marissa to own the bridge and Priyom/Grace for observability and rollback ops.

Next steps: Please confirm the window and who from your team will be on the bridge.

Thanks,

Ben Carter

I'll elevate alert thresholds in advance; primary metrics: p95 latency, error-rate (5xx), connection reset rate, and KV cache-hit %. We'll post the exact threshold list to the drive this afternoon.
- DocuSign for maintenance SLA adjustment: https://app.docusign.com/link/RED-MLA-4492 (expires 72 hours)
- SOC2 artifacts: attaching kestrel-soc2-evidence.zip (contains network ACL screenshots, retention policy excerpt, and audit log export instructions)

Canary thresholds (TL;DR):
- p95 increase <= +20% over baseline
- error-rate <= 1.0% absolute
- sustained connection resets < 0.5% of requests

Operational notes for the bridge:
- Marissa will be primary bridge owner; Grace will watch KV cache warm-up and prefix caching; I'll handle dashboarding/fallback triggers and initiate rollback automation if thresholds breached.

Forwarding the runbook excerpt below for visibility.
